payload.title: Two always-run invariant specs read only the frozen findings.jsonl: finding-id-aliases.spec.ts judges aliases against the genesis ids alone and finding-evidence-shape.spec.ts checks genesis rows alone, so event-born findings and AMENDED evidence fall outside both
evidence: tests/invariants/finding-id-aliases.spec.ts:73-83 (the canonical-exists and no-shadow checks use that id set)
tests/invariants/finding-id-aliases.spec.ts:139-152 (the reissue check claims the same partial set)
tools/gates/finding-registry-projection.ts:394-396 (readRegistryRows, the reader that folds genesis and events)
payload.rule_violated: CLAUDE.md one owner per concept (MF-DESIGN section 3): the registry is read through the projection (finding-registry-projection.ts), not by a spec's own read of findings.jsonl
payload.notes: An alias whose canonical id is an event-born finding (PROC-MEDIUM-062 has no row in findings.jsonl) fails 'every alias resolves'. An alias spelled like an event-born id passes 'no alias shadows a real ledger id' unnoticed, and the allocator reissue check runs on the same partial set. A finding born after the freeze, or one whose evidence an AMENDED event rewrote, is never held to the evidence-shape contract by the spec; only the write-time sink covers it. Latent today: no alias names a post-freeze id. ARIA-MEDIUM-962 does not cover either spec, since it names only the kernel readers. Close condition: Both specs take their rows from readRegistryRows. Tests with an alias to an event-born id (resolves), an alias equal to an event-born id (caught as a shadow), and an event-born row with non-canonical evidence (flagged).
